For a normal Crisis, primary strength uses the normal attack calculation plus local unrest; a Foreign Invasion uses the ordinary die for attack strength without adding unrest to primary strength. An Invasion Crisis compares the attacker’s whole empire strength plus event modifier against the defender’s whole empire strength and succeeds only if strictly greater; a Rebellion compares only the rebelling region’s strength plus modifier against its sovereign capital’s strength, also requiring strictly greater. If the Commander is vacant, Military Affairs acts in their stead, or the Chairman if Military Affairs is vacant; that player chooses defense pieces and gets no trophies. grades.observed_answer: At the start of Revenue, before Company revenue, firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of their share count or firm Value. They may use either or both treasuries. If unable to pay, the firm dissolves unless rescued. On dissolution, its shares go to Debtor’s Prison and each costs -1 VP, ships return to shipyards, and the charter returns to family side; invested workshops stay invested. Emergency investments follow the usual Company-share/workshop rules, even if the ten-share cap prevents new shares; they pay expenses, any remaining money is lost, and firm Value falls one space per emergency investment. Alternatively, the firm may merge with one other firm, which must first pay its own expenses if not already paid and then cover the endangered firm’s unpaid expenses. After expenses, the manager may pay dividends from India treasury only. Each dividend pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to the manager; with manager consent, a shareholder may forgo payment on any number of their shares. Record the total actual cash paid out, rather than a per-share amount, with the dividend cube on the Company Balance track. An active non-Hobnob firm paying none records zero; Hobnob retains its prior marker. Sweep remaining India funds into London treasury.
